`resetall
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none

module arbiter #(
    parameter PORTS = 4,
    parameter ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN = 0,
    parameter ARB_BLOCK = 0,
    parameter ARB_BLOCK_ACK = 1,
    parameter ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY = 0
)(
    input  wire                     clk,
    input  wire                     rst,
    input  wire [PORTS-1:0]         request,
    input  wire [PORTS-1:0]         acknowledge,
    output wire [PORTS-1:0]         grant,
    output wire                     grant_valid,
    output wire [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] grant_encoded
);

reg [PORTS-1:0] grant_reg = 0;
reg grant_valid_reg = 0;
reg [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] grant_encoded_reg = 0;
reg [PORTS-1:0] mask_reg = 0;

assign grant = grant_reg;
assign grant_valid = grant_valid_reg;
assign grant_encoded = grant_encoded_reg;

wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_request = request & mask_reg;
wire request_valid = |request;
wire masked_request_valid = |masked_request;

// Each bit indicates whether a higher-priority request exists.
// These same prefixes are the round-robin masks after selection.
wire [PORTS-1:0] request_prefix;
wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_prefix;
wire [PORTS-1:0] request_winner;
wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_winner;

genvar p, b;
generate
    for (p = 0; p < PORTS; p = p + 1) begin : priority_bits
        if (ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : lsb_first
            if (p == 0) begin : boundary
                assign request_prefix[p] = 1'b0;
                assign masked_prefix[p] = 1'b0;
            end else begin : interior
                assign request_prefix[p] = |request[p-1:0];
                assign masked_prefix[p] = |masked_request[p-1:0];
            end
        end else begin : msb_first
            if (p == PORTS-1) begin : boundary
                assign request_prefix[p] = 1'b0;
                assign masked_prefix[p] = 1'b0;
            end else begin : interior
                assign request_prefix[p] = |request[PORTS-1:p+1];
                assign masked_prefix[p] = |masked_request[PORTS-1:p+1];
            end
        end
        assign request_winner[p] = request[p] & ~request_prefix[p];
        assign masked_winner[p] = masked_request[p] & ~masked_prefix[p];
    end
endgenerate

wire hold_grant = ARB_BLOCK &&
    (ARB_BLOCK_ACK ? (grant_valid_reg && !(|(grant_reg & acknowledge))) :
                     (|(grant_reg & request)));

wire use_masked = ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN && masked_request_valid;
wire take_masked = !hold_grant && use_masked;
wire take_request = !hold_grant && !use_masked && request_valid;

wire [PORTS-1:0] selected_grant =
    ({PORTS{take_masked}} & masked_winner) |
    ({PORTS{take_request}} & request_winner);

wire [PORTS-1:0] grant_next =
    ({PORTS{hold_grant}} & grant_reg) | selected_grant;
wire grant_valid_next =
    (hold_grant && grant_valid_reg) || (!hold_grant && request_valid);

wire [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] selected_encoded;
wire [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] grant_encoded_next;
generate
    for (b = 0; b < $clog2(PORTS); b = b + 1) begin : encode_bits
        wire [PORTS-1:0] terms;
        for (p = 0; p < PORTS; p = p + 1) begin : encode_terms
            if ((p >> b) & 1) begin : index_one
                assign terms[p] = selected_grant[p];
            end else begin : index_zero
                assign terms[p] = 1'b0;
            end
        end
        assign selected_encoded[b] = |terms;
        assign grant_encoded_next[b] =
            (hold_grant & grant_encoded_reg[b]) | selected_encoded[b];
    end
endgenerate

wire update_mask = ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN && !hold_grant && request_valid;
wire [PORTS-1:0] mask_next =
    ({PORTS{!update_mask}} & mask_reg) |
    ({PORTS{ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN && take_masked}} & masked_prefix) |
    ({PORTS{ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN && take_request}} & request_prefix);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst) begin
        grant_reg <= 0;
        grant_valid_reg <= 0;
        grant_encoded_reg <= 0;
        mask_reg <= 0;
    end else begin
        grant_reg <= grant_next;
        grant_valid_reg <= grant_valid_next;
        grant_encoded_reg <= grant_encoded_next;
        mask_reg <= mask_next;
    end
end

endmodule

  "bottleneck": "The supplied STA shows approximately 2.07 ns arrival time on the worst register-to-register path, with substantial combinational depth and buffering. Exact source correspondence is unavailable. A likely structural contributor is the original round-robin feedback through priority encoding, index-dependent mask shifting, selection, and register control.",
  "rewrite": "Replace the top-level encoder uses with parallel priority-prefix reductions. Derive one-hot winners directly from request bits and higher-priority prefixes. Reuse those prefixes as the next round-robin mask, eliminating the encoded-index arithmetic and variable shifts entirely. Generate grant_encoded with an OR encoding of the selected one-hot winner. Express hold and arbitration selection as mutually exclusive terms. The frozen helper module is neither modified nor redefined.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Unmeasured. The intended improvement is a shorter mask-register feedback path: masked request, prefix reduction, selection, and register input instead of priority encoding followed by index arithmetic and mask shifting. Prefix fanout, selection control, or the output encoding may become limiting. Compare mapped WNS against the supplied 7.80 ns baseline under the identical EDA settings before accepting the candidate.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Overlapping prefix reductions may increase logic duplication, routing, or buffering, although synthesis can share reductions and removes the original mask-shift logic. Register count and output latency are unchanged. Mapped area must be checked against the 4880.43072 um2 cap; compliance has not been measured.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the original parameter names/defaults, port widths and signedness, declaration initialization, single positive-edge clock, and active-high synchronous reset. For arbitrary multi-bit requests, each winner is the highest-priority asserted bit. Its next mask equals the corresponding higher-priority-request prefix vector. Masked requests take precedence only in round-robin mode; blocking retains grant, validity, encoded grant, and mask exactly as before. No-request cycles clear the grant outputs unless held and retain the mask. Reset remains effective on every edge, including after startup. No added assumptions, state stages, helper definitions, or latency changes. Formal equivalence against the frozen original under the fixed startup contract and specified overrides remains required."
}
